items.q: Thick, strong roots help hold the tree in place.
Most tree roots grow very deep.
The organic layer is made of fallen leaves and tiny twigs.
Topsoil is often light because it contains decayed plants.
There are more roots and living creatures in the subsoil.
Bedrock is solid rock beneath the soil.
What do the thin, tiny roots do?
options: They take in water and nutrients
items.why: “These tiny roots take in water and nutrients from the soil.”

items.q: What helps break down dead plants?
items.why: “Earthworms, fungi, and tiny creatures help break down dead plants.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Under a tree there is a hidden world of roots, soil and rocks. The soil has layers: the organic layer, the topsoil, the subsoil and the parent material. At the bottom is the bedrock, which is solid rock.

items.q: What do earthworms do in the soil?
items.model: They help break down dead plants, and they dig tunnels that help air and water move underground.

items.q: How is the subsoil different from the topsoil?
items.model: The topsoil is often dark and has many tiny roots. The subsoil is often lighter. It has minerals and clay, and fewer roots and living creatures.
Rainwater, temperature changes and living things.
